In October, 1977 the City of San Jose Department of Property and Code Enforcement, Housing Division, published a document entitled Neighborhood Profiles. This report was prepared to assist in the planning undertaken by city staff and the CDBG Steering Committee in choosing the programs and neighborhoods for funding in the 1978-1979 CDBG Program Year. Because of the lack of recent comprehensive analysis of the conditions of San Jose's critical neighborhoods, the 1977 Neighborhood Profiles study was undertaken. The report was intended to provide the basic data needed to evaluate each area and its problems. In preparing the study available housing condition data and median income of neighborhoods were evaluated. Only those neighborhoods with a substandardness rate less than the estimated city-wide rate of 6.5% (later revised to 5.27%) were investigated. Areas where the median income exceeded 120% of the city's median ($17,233 in 1975 figures-the prevailing government index of moderate income) were eliminated. During on-site visual inspections of housing condition, five aspects of each unit's exterior were evaluated from the street; exterior walls, roof, paint, foundation and porch. A rating system of points was used to determine the overall condition of the house. (refer to Appendix C)
The findings of the Neighborhood Profile are given below. In the cases of Mayfair, Alma, Alviso, and Gardner the boundaries of the selected CNRAs and the neighborhoods analyzed in the Profile are co-terminus. The description which follows each of these CNRA's is divided into sub-areas as reflected in the Profile research. The Olinder and Northside CNRA's are included within larger areas studied by the Neighborhood Profile. The data which was assembled and analyzed does not relate exactly to the boundaries later used to define Northside and Olinder. The information provided below, then, refers to larger geographic area within which the specific Northside and Olinder neighborhoods, as defined in the CDBG program occur. No specific information was gathered for the Campus CNRA, as defined by the CDBG plan. Data presented herein is from a study currently in progress by the City of San Jose Property and Code Enforcement Department.
Alma CNRA:
Location
Located in the Central Planning Area, the Alma neighborhood is bounded by Alma Avenue, Monterey Highway, San Jose Avenue and Little Orchard.
Summary and Recommendations
The substandardness rate in this neighborhood is critical, the highest of the areas surveyed. Major substandard conditions were identified for 53% of the area. The median income of the census tract is very low and a significant portion of the residents are elderly. Street emprovements are required throughout the area.
